clue.text: Eyebrow raising writer

blocks.note: surface reading: something shocking that makes people raise their eyebrows
setter's reading: a writing tool that, in make-up, is used to draw the eyebrows higher

explanation.surface: An author whose work scandalises readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eyebrow raising' looks like the adjective 'shocking', but it describes the make-up use of an eyebrow pencil, which also writes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pencil is a simple writing instrument, and an eyebrow pencil is the cosmetic stick used to shape and lift brows.

clue.text: The advantage being sharp gives one

blocks.note: first meaning: a slight lead over rivals
second meaning: a keen blade has a cutting rim

explanation.surface: Being quick-witted gives you a lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the upper hand is having the edge, and a sharpened blade has a fine cutting edge.

clue.text: Look round for a way to throw a fight

blocks.note: to cast is to throw
taken as written
a bout is a boxing match

explanation.surface: Searching for a method of fixing a boxing match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throw a fight' suggests losing on purpose, but here it is read word by word.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast about is to search around in various directions, especially for a means or plan.

clue.text: Tiny raised inlay that may have to be made up

definitions.text: that may have to be made up

indicators.note: in a down entry, 'raised' lifts the word upward so it reads bottom to top
'in' puts the preceding word inside the one that follows

blocks.note: wee is Scottish and informal for tiny
the word splits into in + lay; lay is taken as written, and in is the insertion signal

explanation.surface: A tiny raised decoration set into a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is lost time or ground, a deficit one may have to make up, originally a ship's sideways drift.

clue.text: Indecision shows us soft in reason

indicators.note: 'in' places the preceding letters inside the word for reason

blocks.note: sense, as in good judgment or reason
taken as written
p (piano) is the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: Someone's dithering reveals that we are being weak in our thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is a state of uncertainty, of waiting with a decision or outcome still unsettled.

clue.text: Fishmonger having a monopoly?

blocks.note: surface reading: the only trader allowed to sell goods
setter's reading: one who supplies a particular flatfish

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a pun: the flatfish shares its name with the word for 'only'.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm with exclusive supply rights is the only distributor; a fishmonger selling the flatfish fits literally.

clue.text: Play to the balcony

blocks.note: surface reading: performing for the cheap seats in a theatre's upper tier
setter's reading: the window ledge where a beloved stands, as Juliet does

explanation.walkthrough: 'Play to the balcony' suggests theatre acting to the gallery, but it is a lover singing up to a window.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is music sung or played at night outside a sweetheart's window.

clue.text: Peg-legged supporter of the Arts

blocks.note: surface reading: a patron of culture with a wooden leg
setter's reading: a stand on wooden legs, with pegs to hold a painter's canvas

explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' suggests a sponsor or patron, but it is a physical stand used by painters.
explanation.definitionFit: Artists rest canvases on a wooden tripod stand, adjusted with pegs, while painting.

clue.text: The second mate raising the issue?

definitions.text: The second mate raising the issue?

blocks.clueFragment: The second mate raising the issue?
blocks.note: surface reading: a ship's officer bringing up a matter for discussion
setter's reading: a later wife bringing up her husband's children from a former marriage

explanation.walkthrough: A second mate is a ship's officer, and raising an issue is mentioning it; here issue means offspring and mate means spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A father's new wife becomes parent by marriage to his existing children, helping bring them up.

clue.text: Type of porcelain food container

blocks.note: first meaning: very thin, delicate china
second meaning: the casing round an egg's contents

explanation.surface: A kind of china used for holding food.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggshell porcelain is a fine translucent china, and the literal shell is what holds an egg's edible contents.

clue.text: Condition of tank, perhaps, after attack from the air

definitions.text: Condition of tank, perhaps, after attack from the air

blocks.clueFragment: Condition of tank, perhaps, after attack from the air
blocks.note: surface reading: a military tank damaged by bombing from aircraft
setter's reading: the slow chemical attack of oxygen and moisture on a metal water tank

explanation.surface: A battlefield report on an armoured vehicle after an air raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attack from the air' suggests bombers, but it is oxidation: air corrodes an iron tank.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron exposed to oxygen and moisture corrodes, leaving a metal tank coated with reddish oxide.

clue.text: Magic lantern -  a feature of Christmas entertainment?

blocks.note: first meaning: the enchanted lamp holding a genie in the Arabian Nights
second meaning: a prop in the pantomime Aladdin, a staple of British Christmas theatre

explanation.surface: A slide projector being part of a festive show.
explanation.walkthrough: A magic lantern was an early slide projector; here it is a literal enchanted lamp. Pantomime is a British Christmas stage show, and Aladdin is one of its stock stories.
explanation.definitionFit: The genie's lamp in the tale is truly enchanted, and it appears in every staging of the Aladdin pantomime each December.

clue.text: Business residence

blocks.note: first meaning: one's job or trade
second meaning: the act of living in a property

explanation.definitionFit: An occupation is a job or line of work, and occupation of a house is living in it as a tenant.

clue.text: Classical maid who always had the last word

definitions.text: Classical maid who always had the last word

blocks.clueFragment: Classical maid who always had the last word
blocks.note: surface reading: an argumentative young woman from antiquity who never let anyone else finish
setter's reading: the nymph cursed to repeat only the final words spoken to her

explanation.surface: A quarrelsome girl of Greek legend who always won the argument.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Hera punished this nymph so she could only repeat the ends of others' sentences.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythological nymph could only speak by repeating others' closing words, which is how reflected sound got its name.

clue.text: Not the main road from Spithead

indicators.note: 'from' signals that the answer is made out of the letters of the following place name, rearranged

blocks.note: Spithead is the stretch of water off Portsmouth used as a naval anchorage

explanation.surface: Directions for a minor route leading away from a coastal spot near Portsmouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a mild anagram signal: the answer is made from the place name's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A side path is a minor track branching off, as opposed to the principal highway.

clue.text: Punishment escaped by unnamed soldiers

blocks.note: surface reading: anonymous troops who avoided being disciplined
setter's reading: the army saying that if no names are given, nobody is punished

explanation.walkthrough: It draws on the British saying 'no names, no pack drill': if nobody is named, nobody gets punished.
explanation.definitionFit: Pack drill was a military punishment of marching up and down in full kit.

clue.text: Not a fatal disease, but one I'm to peg out from

indicators.note: 'peg out' hides 'out', meaning the letters are put out of their order

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient reassured that this illness won't kill them, even if they fear dying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peg out' is British slang for die, which plays against 'Not a fatal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetigo is a contagious bacterial skin infection, unpleasant but rarely dangerous.

clue.text: Maybe more cuts will attract one

indicators.note: 'Maybe' says the following letters might be arranged otherwise

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper reasons that further price reductions will bring in a buyer.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also reads as a shop's logic: price cuts draw in shoppers. 'one' is the definition, the person attracted.
explanation.definitionFit: 'One' stands for a person, here the buyer whom discounts lure into a shop.

clue.text: Potting aids

blocks.note: surface reading: gardening tools for putting plants into pots
setter's reading: sinking balls in snooker or billiards

explanation.walkthrough: 'Potting' suggests the garden shed, but in snooker you pot a ball into a pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Players strike balls with long tapered sticks, the tools that make sinking balls on a snooker table possible.

clue.text: Lifting service inaccurate, well out

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the Royal Air Force is one of the armed services
off, as in wide of the mark

explanation.surface: An aircraft lift service that is wildly mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Far-off describes something distant, a long way away, just as 'well out' means remote.

clue.text: The chairman of the directors could be in deep water

definitions.text: The chairman of the directors could be in deep water

blocks.clueFragment: The chairman of the directors could be in deep water
blocks.note: surface reading: a company head in serious trouble
setter's reading: a person set above a board, which read literally is the cry for someone fallen from a ship

explanation.surface: A company chief facing serious trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In deep water' sounds like business trouble, but it is literal sea; the chairman is a person placed over the board.
explanation.definitionFit: The shout raised when someone falls from a vessel into the sea, punning on a person above a board of directors.

clue.text: Board has positive answers from two European states

blocks.clueFragment: positive answers from two European states
blocks.note: oui is French for yes

blocks.clueFragment: positive answers from two European states
blocks.note: ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: A committee receives approval from two countries.
explanation.walkthrough: The board's trade name is French and German for yes put together.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ouija board is a lettered board used at seances to spell supposed spirit messages.

clue.text: Measure of night-time temperature

indicators.note: 'of' says the answer is made of letters lying in the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A reading of the temperature after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: To mete is an old verb meaning to measure or to allot, as in meting out punishment.

clue.text: Pacific island in which a girl may be found  sunbathing

definitions.text: in which a girl may be found  sunbathing

blocks.note: first meaning: the Marshall Islands atoll used for nuclear tests

blocks.clueFragment: in which a girl may be found  sunbathing
blocks.note: second meaning: the two-piece swimsuit named after that atoll

explanation.surface: A tropical island where young women lie on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Bikini Atoll lies in the Pacific, and the skimpy two-piece swimming costume took its name from it.

clue.text: Deceives more than once

blocks.note: first meaning: is unfaithful to a partner
second meaning: literally twice

explanation.surface: Someone cheats again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: To two-time is to cheat on a lover with someone else, and read literally the phrase means on two occasions.

clue.text: Popular pro

blocks.note: first meaning: well liked, enjoying approval
second meaning: supporting, on the side of

explanation.surface: A well-liked professional.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in favour enjoys others' approval, and to be in favour of something is to support it.

clue.text: Strain that's a trifle  unexpected

indicators.note: 'unexpected' says the preceding letters come out in a surprising new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A slight, surprising muscle strain or tension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' looks like an injury noun, but it is the verb meaning to sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: To strain a liquid is to pass it through a sieve or mesh, separating out solids.
